content.value_statement: Distributed .NET services need reliable messaging patterns that are easy to implement correctly. This skill guides Azure Service Bus queues, topics, sessions, and processing.
actual_capabilities: Explains package installation and required environment values.
Shows Microsoft Entra ID and connection string client setup.
Covers sending, receiving, settlement, and background processors.
Describes sessions, dead letter queues, topics, subscriptions, and administration.
Lists best practices for disposal, batching, transient errors, and transport options.
limitations: Does not provision Azure resources outside the shown examples.
Does not validate your namespace, credentials, or network access.
Does not replace an Azure security review for production systems.
Examples may need changes for your SDK version and application architecture.

use_cases.title: Add Queue Messaging
use_cases.description: Implement reliable queue send and receive flows in a .NET application.

use_cases.title: Design Event Distribution
use_cases.description: Use topics and subscriptions to distribute business events across services.

use_cases.title: Operate Background Workers
use_cases.description: Build processors that handle settlement, retries, dead letters, and ordered sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Send and Receive
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a queue workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to send and receive one Azure Service Bus message in .NET using Microsoft Entra ID.

prompt_templates.title: Process Queue Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a .NET worker pattern that processes queue messages, handles errors, and completes messages only after success.

prompt_templates.title: Model Pub/Sub
prompt_templates.prompt: Design topic and subscription usage for order events, including filtering, dead lettering, and retry behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Service Bus .NET design for sessions, transactions, batching, lock duration, and production risks.

output_examples.input: I need a queue producer and consumer for a .NET service.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with authentication choice, client lifetime guidance, send flow, receive flow, and settlement behavior.

output_examples.input: My messages must be processed in order for each order.
output_examples.output: A session-based design explaining session IDs, session receivers, lock renewal, and state management.

output_examples.input: I need to handle failed messages after retries.
output_examples.output: A dead letter handling approach with failure reasons, inspection steps, replay guidance, and operational checks.

best_practices: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID and managed identity over connection strings.
Use processors and explicit settlement for background message handling.
Test dead letter, retry, and lock renewal behavior before production rollout.
anti_patterns: Do not create a new ServiceBusClient for every message.
Do not complete messages before durable processing succeeds.
Do not store connection strings in source code or prompts.

faq.question: What SDK does this skill cover?
Can it help with managed identity?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Microsoft Entra ID with DefaultAzureCredential for production authentication.

faq.question: Does it cover topics and subscriptions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for sending to topics and receiving from subscriptions.

faq.question: Does it explain dead letter queues?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows settlement, dead lettering, metadata inspection, and recovery concepts.

faq.question: Can it design ordered processing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Service Bus sessions for FIFO processing within a session.

faq.question: Does it replace Azure documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes practical patterns and links official references for deeper details.
